neetpg2021-q001: Night blindness, dry eyes (xerophthalmia), gritty sensation and corneal softening (keratomalacia) are due to vitamin A deficiency. Retinoic acid is the form of vitamin A that acts in epithelial differentiation, and retinal is needed for rhodopsin.
neetpg2021-q002: Rifampicin is a strong inducer of hepatic cytochrome P450 (CYP3A4), which speeds up the metabolism of oestrogen and progestin in oral contraceptive pills. This can cause contraceptive failure, so an additional barrier method is advised.
neetpg2021-q003: Rotenone blocks complex I and antimycin A blocks complex III, so succinate would bypass rotenone. Oligomycin inhibits ATP synthase (complex V), which stops respiration in coupled mitochondria. 2,4-dinitrophenol uncouples and increases oxygen consumption.
neetpg2021-q004: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers are teratogenic (renal dysgenesis, oligohydramnios, skull defects) and are stopped before conception. Labetalol, nifedipine and methyldopa are safe in pregnancy.
neetpg2021-q005: Indomethacin inhibits prostaglandin synthesis, and prostaglandins keep the ductus arteriosus open, so use in pregnancy can cause premature closure of the ductus, with oligohydramnios. Indomethacin is also used to close a PDA in neonates.
neetpg2021-q006: Tendon xanthomas, raised total cholesterol and LDL with a good response to statins indicate familial hypercholesterolaemia (LDL receptor defect, type IIa). Chylomicron disorders raise triglycerides, not LDL.
neetpg2021-q007: Latanoprost, a prostaglandin F2 alpha analogue, lowers intraocular pressure and is safe in asthma. Timolol is a non-selective beta-blocker that can precipitate bronchospasm. Mannitol is for acute angle closure.
neetpg2021-q008: Alprazolam is a Schedule H1 drug in India. Of the options, the key gives 0.5 mg once daily at bedtime for 7 days. Benzodiazepines are prescribed in the lowest dose for the shortest duration to limit dependence.
neetpg2021-q009: Keratan sulfate is the main glycosaminoglycan of the cornea, and its regular arrangement with collagen maintains transparency. Dermatan sulfate is also found in the cornea.
neetpg2021-q010: ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril cause angioedema, with swelling of lips and face, due to bradykinin accumulation. Calcium channel blockers like nifedipine cause pedal oedema and gum hyperplasia.
neetpg2021-q011: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase, reducing thromboxane A2 (platelet aggregation) and prostaglandins that protect the gastric mucosa, so it causes gastric erosions and occult GI bleeding. The key lists thromboxane.
neetpg2021-q012: Bisphosphonates (alendronate) are the first-line drugs in osteoporosis and are given for 5 years or more, not just one year. Teriparatide is reserved for severe osteoporosis, and calcium 1200 mg/day with vitamin D is advised. So the false statement is that bisphosphonates are not given for more than a year.
neetpg2021-q013: After an overnight fast (about 11 hours since dinner), blood glucose is maintained by hepatic glycogenolysis for roughly the first 12-18 hours. Gluconeogenesis predominates after 24 hours of fasting. Muscle glycogen cannot release free glucose.
neetpg2021-q014: IV metoclopramide or prochlorperazine can cause acute dystonia (extrapyramidal effects). It is treated with an anticholinergic such as benzhexol (trihexyphenidyl), benztropine or promethazine. Levodopa would worsen it.
neetpg2021-q015: Hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer (Lynch syndrome) results from defects in DNA mismatch repair genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2), with microsatellite instability.
neetpg2021-q016: The maintenance dosing rate equals clearance multiplied by the target plasma concentration (divided by bioavailability for oral doses). Loading dose depends on volume of distribution.
neetpg2021-q017: In homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency, cysteine becomes an essential amino acid because it cannot be made from methionine. Marfanoid habitus, lens subluxation (downward) and thrombosis are seen. Methionine intake is restricted.
neetpg2021-q018: Urine that darkens on standing with joint pain (ochronotic arthritis) is alkaptonuria, due to homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase deficiency. Homogentisic acid accumulates and pigments cartilage.
neetpg2021-q019: Dermatitis in sun-exposed areas, diarrhoea and dementia in a person eating maize (low in available niacin and tryptophan) is pellagra, from niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency.
neetpg2021-q020: Clarithromycin, a macrolide, inhibits P-glycoprotein and gut flora that metabolise digoxin, which raises serum digoxin levels and causes toxicity. Other drugs that raise digoxin include quinidine, verapamil and amiodarone.
neetpg2021-q021: Methotrexate is a folic acid analogue that competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), depleting tetrahydrofolate needed for purine and thymidylate synthesis. High-dose methotrexate with leucovorin rescue is used in osteosarcoma.
neetpg2021-q022: Metronidazole inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, so alcohol causes a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, vomiting, palpitations). Alcohol should be avoided during treatment and for 24-48 hours afterward.
neetpg2021-q023: In chronic kidney disease, NSAIDs (naproxen, indomethacin, diclofenac) reduce renal prostaglandins and further harm the kidney. Paracetamol (acetaminophen) is the safest analgesic.
neetpg2021-q024: A black pigment in hilar lymph nodes is anthracotic pigment (carbon particles inhaled and taken up by macrophages), common in urban dwellers and smokers. It is not a sign of metastasis.
neetpg2021-q025: Fever, pancytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly and macrophages with amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies, with kinetoplast) mean visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar). The vector is the female sandfly (Phlebotomus argentipes).
neetpg2021-q026: Massive splenomegaly with high leukocyte count, basophilia, and myelocytes with a myeloid to erythroid ratio of 18:1 is chronic myeloid leukaemia. The most sensitive test is RT-PCR or FISH for BCR-ABL. Low LAP score supports but is not specific.
neetpg2021-q027: Koplik spots, coryza, conjunctivitis and a descending maculopapular rash are measles. The virus is an enveloped, single-stranded, negative-sense RNA paramyxovirus.
neetpg2021-q028: Short stature, webbed neck, shield chest, increased carrying angle and lymphoedema of the ankles in a girl is Turner syndrome (45,X).
neetpg2021-q029: Nausea and vomiting within 1-6 hours of eating pastries or custard, cream or meat left out are caused by preformed Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxin. B. cereus emetic toxin is typically in fried rice.
neetpg2021-q030: Benzene exposure causes bone marrow damage and increases the risk of leukaemia (acute myeloid), with aplastic anaemia. Bladder cancer is linked to aniline dyes and naphthylamine.
neetpg2021-q031: In iron deficiency anaemia, transferrin saturation falls and ferritin falls, while TIBC, free erythrocyte protoporphyrin and soluble transferrin receptors rise. So transferrin saturation is the exception.
neetpg2021-q032: Selenite F broth is an enrichment medium for Salmonella and Shigella from stool. Alkaline peptone water is for Vibrio cholerae and Robertson cooked meat for clostridia.
neetpg2021-q033: A painless indurated genital ulcer (chancre) is primary syphilis, caused by Treponema pallidum, which is too thin for a light microscope. Its corkscrew motility is seen on dark-field microscopy.
neetpg2021-q034: A high serum beta-2 microglobulin is the strongest prognostic marker in multiple myeloma, and with albumin forms the International Staging System. High beta-2 microglobulin indicates a heavy tumour burden and a poor prognosis.
neetpg2021-q035: Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae are sheathed with a tail tip free of nuclei. Brugia malayi has two terminal nuclei and Loa loa has nuclei right up to the tail tip.
neetpg2021-q036: Turner syndrome has streak gonads (bilateral small streak ovaries) with primary amenorrhoea, along with bicuspid aortic valve and coarctation of the aorta. Aortic dissection is a late complication. Lens subluxation is seen in Marfan syndrome and homocystinuria.
neetpg2021-q037: Pancytopenia with a low reticulocyte count and a hypocellular bone marrow with fat and no immature cells is aplastic anaemia. Marrow in MDS or leukaemia shows blasts or dysplasia.
neetpg2021-q038: A false-negative agglutination test at low serum dilutions with a positive result at higher dilutions is the prozone phenomenon, caused by excess antibody blocking lattice formation. Diluting the serum fixes it.
neetpg2021-q039: Palpable purpura, abdominal pain, arthritis and renal involvement (haematuria, proteinuria) in a child is Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis). Platelet count is normal, unlike ITP.
neetpg2021-q040: Countertransference is the therapist's emotional reaction (conscious or unconscious) to the patient, while transference is the patient's feelings towards the therapist.
neetpg2021-q041: In uterus didelphys complications include abortion, preterm labour, malpresentation (breech) and endometriosis from obstructed hemivagina. Transverse lie is more typical of a septate or arcuate uterus and other conditions, and the key marks it as the exception.
neetpg2021-q042: Agitation, disorientation, visual hallucinations and altered sensorium 48-72 hours after stopping alcohol is delirium tremens, a medical emergency treated with benzodiazepines and thiamine.
neetpg2021-q043: Learning to perform a skill (handwashing steps) belongs to the psychomotor domain of Bloom's taxonomy. Cognitive is knowledge and affective is attitude and values.
neetpg2021-q044: Persistent elevation of hCG after molar evacuation with lung metastases is gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Low-risk disease (FIGO score 6 or less) is treated with methotrexate and folinic acid; high-risk disease (7 or more) needs EMACO. The key marks methotrexate with folinic acid.
neetpg2021-q045: Derailment (loosening of associations) is a formal thought disorder of the form of thought. Delusions, obsessions and thought insertion are disorders of thought content.
neetpg2021-q046: In pregnancy, warfarin is replaced with LMWH or unfractionated heparin before delivery (at 36 weeks) to lower the bleeding risk in the mother and the fetus. With an INR of 3 and a prosthetic valve, the key says stop warfarin and start LMWH.
neetpg2021-q047: Elevated mood, flight of ideas, overfamiliarity and increased sexual desire in a young patient is mania. Hypomania lacks psychotic symptoms and does not impair functioning severely.
neetpg2021-q048: A contrast study of the uterine cavity and tubes, with radiopaque dye seen in the cavity on X-ray, is hysterosalpingography, used to look for uterine anomalies in recurrent miscarriage.
neetpg2021-q049: Leakage of urine on coughing and sneezing is stress urinary incontinence, from weak pelvic floor and urethral support (uterine prolapse with cystocele). Urge incontinence is due to detrusor overactivity.
neetpg2021-q050: A uterine septum causing infertility or recurrent loss is treated by hysteroscopic septum resection (septoplasty). Metroplasty by laparotomy is for bicornuate uterus (Strassman).
neetpg2021-q051: A young man with inflammatory back pain (morning stiffness, improves with exercise), onset before 40 and heel pain (enthesitis) has ankylosing spondylitis. Look for HLA-B27, sacroiliitis and bamboo spine on X-ray.
neetpg2021-q052: Recurrent first-trimester losses, a fetal loss after 10 weeks and early-onset pre-eclampsia with preterm delivery point to antiphospholipid antibody syndrome. Treatment in pregnancy is low-dose aspirin with heparin.
neetpg2021-q053: In a child with knee pain and normal bone density, X-ray features such as a Wimberger ring, Frankel line and Trummerfeld zone point to scurvy (vitamin C deficiency). Rickets shows widened, cupped physes and low bone density.
neetpg2021-q054: Postpartum haemorrhage with transfusion, failure of lactation and persistent amenorrhoea indicate Sheehan syndrome (postpartum pituitary necrosis), with hypothyroidism features such as fatigue and constipation.
neetpg2021-q055: The test shown is a clinical test for a hand nerve. The key marks the median nerve; examples include Phalen's test or the OK sign for the anterior interosseous branch.
neetpg2021-q056: For a suspected uterine anomaly on ultrasound, hysteroscopy with laparoscopy is the gold standard, as it shows both the inside of the cavity and the outer contour of the uterus. HSG and 3D USG are screening tools.
neetpg2021-q057: A progressive swelling around the wrist in an adult with an eccentric lytic lesion at the end of a long bone (distal radius) with a soap-bubble look is osteoclastoma (giant cell tumour), typically at 20-40 years of age.
neetpg2021-q058: Dry hot skin, urinary retention, constipation and delirium after eating a garden fruit is anticholinergic poisoning from Datura. Physostigmine, a cholinesterase inhibitor, is the antidote.
neetpg2021-q059: Infra-umbilical flattening of the abdomen with fetal heart sounds heard on the flanks (lateral side) indicates an occipito-posterior position, as the fetal back is directed posteriorly.
neetpg2021-q060: A flexed, adducted and medially (internally) rotated shortened limb after trauma is posterior dislocation of the hip, the commonest type, as in a dashboard injury. Anterior dislocation gives abduction and external rotation.
neetpg2021-q061: Back pain with morning stiffness, red eyes (uveitis) and bamboo spine on X-ray is ankylosing spondylitis. Syndesmophytes and sacroiliitis are classic.
neetpg2021-q062: A wound with irregular margins, tissue bridging and bruised edges is a laceration. The key marks incised-looking lacerations, which occur over bony prominences like the scalp where skin is thin and tight.
neetpg2021-q063: Active genital herpes lesions at the onset of labour is an indication for an elective caesarean section to prevent neonatal herpes, with acyclovir given to the mother.
neetpg2021-q064: In heat stroke the body temperature is above 40 degrees C, with hot dry skin (no sweating in classical heat stroke), hypotension and altered sensorium. Sweating is the least likely feature.
neetpg2021-q065: Cocaine causes sympathetic stimulation: tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, agitation, coronary vasospasm and ischaemia. Bradycardia goes against the diagnosis.
neetpg2021-q066: A woman with large intramural fibroids at the cornual ends (blocking the tubes) and infertility with a normal semen analysis is treated with myomectomy to restore fertility. Embolisation and GnRH analogues are not advised when pregnancy is desired.
neetpg2021-q067: Maceration of the skin of the hands, with washerwoman's hands, in a body kept in water for about 36 hours is the image. In warm water changes occur faster and cutis anserina appears early.
neetpg2021-q068: A diffuse effacement of the lymph node by atypical centrocytes and centroblasts with CD10 and BCL2 positivity is follicular lymphoma, t(14;18). Burkitt lymphoma is CD10 positive but BCL2 negative.
neetpg2021-q069: Copious, non-itchy clear vaginal discharge around mid-cycle (day 13) is physiological, due to the oestrogen peak at ovulation. This is cervical mucus and needs no treatment.
neetpg2021-q070: In atonic PPH the stepwise devascularisation is: uterine artery ligation, then ovarian (utero-ovarian) artery ligation, then internal iliac artery ligation. Hysterectomy is the final step.
neetpg2021-q071: The nuts shown are Semecarpus anacardium (marking nut), whose active principle is bhilawanol, a vesicant. Ricin is from castor, abrin from Abrus precatorius, and calotropin from Calotropis.
neetpg2021-q072: Hb 9 g/dL with MCV 80 fL and a poor diet low in fruits and vegetables suggests early iron deficiency anaemia (the mean cell volume is still borderline). Deficiency of B12 or folate gives a macrocytic picture.
neetpg2021-q073: A transverse vaginal septum causes obstruction to menstrual flow, leading to retrograde menstruation, so endometriosis is the commonest complication, along with haematocolpos.
neetpg2021-q074: Greenish discolouration of the skin over the abdomen (right iliac fossa) is due to sulfhaemoglobin formed by bacterial putrefaction, appearing in 24 to 36 hours, and spreading with marbling. The cause is bacterial, not aseptic.
neetpg2021-q075: G is the number of pregnancies including the current one, and P the number of deliveries after viability. Twins delivered together count as one parity. So she is G2P1.
neetpg2021-q076: Eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in hepatocytes of alcoholic hepatitis are Mallory-Denk bodies, made of aggregated intermediate filaments (prekeratin or cytokeratin 8 and 18).
neetpg2021-q077: Obtaining sexual gratification from exposing oneself to strangers is exhibitionism. Voyeurism is watching others who are undressed, and fetishism involves objects.
neetpg2021-q078: This answer in the key is to discard the pack and start a new pack with an alternate contraceptive. In general, missing several pills in a pack raises the risk of pregnancy, so backup contraception is needed.
neetpg2021-q079: Superfecundation is fertilisation of two ova released in the same cycle by sperm from two different acts of intercourse (often with different fathers), giving twins with different fathers. Superfetation is a second conception in a later cycle.
neetpg2021-q080: A woman with an unruptured ectopic pregnancy, hCG under 5000 mIU/mL and no fetal cardiac activity, who is stable, is managed with single-dose methotrexate (50 mg/m2 IM). Surgery is for rupture or instability.
neetpg2021-q081: A question that suggests its own answer, as 'Did A kill B in your presence?', is a leading question. It is allowed in cross-examination but not in examination-in-chief or re-examination without permission.
neetpg2021-q082: Dating by the LMP is unreliable in a woman who recently stopped oral contraceptives, so crown-rump length on first-trimester ultrasound is the best method, accurate to within 5-7 days.
neetpg2021-q083: Infantile pyloric stenosis causes persistent non-bilious projectile vomiting with loss of hydrochloric acid and potassium. This gives hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis. A paradoxical aciduria develops in later stages.
neetpg2021-q084: Rickets resistant to vitamin D, with low phosphate, normal calcium and PTH, and a normal renal function and ABG, indicates hypophosphataemic rickets (X-linked dominant, PHEX mutation). It is treated with phosphate and calcitriol.
neetpg2021-q085: Height for age below -2 SD indicates stunting, a marker of chronic undernutrition. Weight for height below -2 SD indicates wasting (acute malnutrition).
neetpg2021-q086: Headache that is worse with regular use of analgesics for several months and improves on stopping them is medication overuse headache, treated by withdrawing the offending drug.
neetpg2021-q087: Pure red cell aplasia with a mediastinal mass is associated with thymoma, an autoimmune cause. Thymoma is also associated with myasthenia gravis and hypogammaglobulinaemia.
neetpg2021-q088: Generalised oedema, heavy proteinuria (3+), hypercholesterolaemia and fat bodies (oval fat bodies) in the urine is nephrotic syndrome. Nephritic syndrome has haematuria, hypertension and oliguria.
neetpg2021-q089: A child with a VP shunt who develops signs of meningitis should have blood cultures and CSF taken by shunt tap (shunt infection). Lumbar puncture may not reflect ventricular CSF and carries a risk.
neetpg2021-q090: Mitral stenosis with atrial fibrillation needs long-term anticoagulation with a vitamin K antagonist (warfarin), because the direct oral anticoagulants are not recommended for rheumatic mitral stenosis.
neetpg2021-q091: Two umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated fetal blood from the internal iliac arteries to the placenta. The umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus.
neetpg2021-q092: A mild mid-diastolic murmur with prominent a waves in the JVP, due to forceful right atrial contraction against a stenosed valve, indicates tricuspid stenosis. In mitral stenosis the JVP is normal unless there is pulmonary hypertension.
neetpg2021-q093: A school-age child with seizures and a history of measles at 1 year has subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. Diagnosis is by raised measles IgG antibody in the CSF, with a typical EEG pattern.
neetpg2021-q094: In a cirrhotic with ascites and rising creatinine, hepatorenal syndrome is likely. Treatment is IV albumin with vasoconstrictors, such as terlipressin, octreotide plus midodrine, or noradrenaline. Diuretics are stopped.
neetpg2021-q095: A 68-year-old with pneumonia, stable and not confused, with urea 44 mg/dL (about 7 mmol/L) scores 2 on CURB-65 (urea and age 65). This calls for hospital admission in a non-ICU ward.
neetpg2021-q096: Fatigue that improves with rest and worsens by evening, with ptosis, dysarthria and dysphagia, is myasthenia gravis, an autoantibody disease of the acetylcholine receptors. Lambert-Eaton improves with exercise.
neetpg2021-q097: A 16-month-old boy weighing 8 kg is below the -2 SD line on the WHO weight-for-age chart, i.e. underweight. The key says moderate malnutrition, managed by teaching the mother feeding practices.
neetpg2021-q098: Hyperventilation blows off CO2, causing respiratory alkalosis. Alkalosis reduces ionised calcium and causes tetany and carpopedal spasm.
neetpg2021-q099: The drug shown is a topical agent in the airway: the key says it is used in subglottic stenosis (mitomycin C, applied topically to reduce scar formation).
neetpg2021-q100: Difficulty breathing and failed extubation after total thyroidectomy is due to bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve injury, causing bilateral vocal cord paralysis in the adducted position. Unilateral injury gives hoarseness. Haematoma presents with neck swelling.
neetpg2021-q101: Recurrent chest infections and greasy, bulky stools with fat above 10 g/day indicate pancreatic insufficiency from cystic fibrosis. Distal intestinal obstruction syndrome (meconium ileus equivalent) is a recognised complication. Protein-losing enteropathy is not typical.
neetpg2021-q102: Foul-smelling discharge, yellow-green crusts, loss of smell and a wide, atrophic nasal cavity is atrophic rhinitis (ozaena), with a roomy nasal cavity due to turbinate atrophy. Klebsiella ozaenae is associated.
neetpg2021-q103: A young woman with claudication in the arms, absent or weak femoral pulses, visual loss and retinal changes has Takayasu arteritis (pulseless disease), a granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis of the aorta and its branches.
neetpg2021-q104: An aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery compresses the optic chiasma, causing bitemporal field defects. Posterior communicating artery aneurysms cause a third nerve palsy.
neetpg2021-q105: For persistent epistaxis despite anterior packing, the next step is posterior packing or endoscopic ligation of the sphenopalatine artery, the main supply of the posterior nasal cavity. External carotid ligation is a later step.
neetpg2021-q106: Persistent vomiting causes loss of hydrochloric acid, leading to metabolic alkalosis with hypochloraemia and hypokalaemia. DKA would produce a metabolic acidosis with a raised anion gap.
neetpg2021-q107: Nocturnal cough, wheeze, very high eosinophil count (above 5000/microL) and miliary mottling on chest X-ray is tropical pulmonary eosinophilia from filarial infection. It is treated with diethylcarbamazine.
neetpg2021-q108: The phrenicocolic ligament supports the splenic flexure of the colon and forms a shelf for the lower pole of the spleen, so an enlarged spleen is kept from sliding down. The question also relates to the spleen's long axis along the 10th rib.
neetpg2021-q109: Circumvallate papillae are large, dome-shaped papillae lined by a deep circular trench, with taste buds on the walls and serous (von Ebner) glands opening in the trench. They lie in front of the sulcus terminalis.
neetpg2021-q110: Multiple humerus fractures with difficulty in elbow flexion and forearm supination and loss of sensation over the lateral forearm is a musculocutaneous nerve injury (biceps brachii and brachialis).
neetpg2021-q111: Peaked (tented) T waves in a dialysis patient indicate hyperkalaemia, which is associated with metabolic acidosis. Laboured breathing is Kussmaul respiration, giving a low pH, a low pCO2 (respiratory compensation) and a low HCO3.
neetpg2021-q112: Tight skin on the face, Raynaud's phenomenon (numb fingertips) and a nucleolar ANA pattern point to systemic sclerosis. Anti-Scl 70 gives a speckled pattern and anticentromere antibodies point to limited disease (CREST).
neetpg2021-q113: The lingual nerve lies close to the submandibular gland and duct and is at risk during resection, along with the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve and the hypoglossal nerve. The key marks the lingual nerve.
neetpg2021-q114: In a hypertensive patient with chest pain, collapse and unequal pulses, aortic dissection should be suspected. In an unstable patient the bedside investigation of choice is transoesophageal echocardiography.
neetpg2021-q115: The great saphenous vein is accompanied by the saphenous nerve (branch of the femoral nerve) below the knee, which supplies the medial side of the leg and foot. It is at risk during vein harvesting.
neetpg2021-q116: Bronchial breathing and crepitations with lobar consolidation in an HIV-positive child with productive cough is most commonly due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, the commonest bacterial pneumonia in HIV. PCP gives diffuse interstitial infiltrates with dry cough.
neetpg2021-q117: Seizure with low serum osmolality (270) and inappropriately concentrated urine (1000) indicates SIADH, causing hyponatraemia. Severe hyponatraemia causes seizures.
neetpg2021-q118: Weak femoral pulses with upper limb hypertension and rib notching (enlarged intercostal collaterals) is coarctation of the aorta. A bicuspid aortic valve is a common association.
neetpg2021-q119: After coronary stenting, dual antiplatelet therapy is needed: aspirin plus a P2Y12 receptor blocker (clopidogrel, prasugrel or ticagrelor), to prevent stent thrombosis. Anticoagulants are not first choice here.
neetpg2021-q120: Reactionary or primary bleeding after tonsillectomy in the recovery room is managed by returning to theatre, removing the clots and securing the bleeding point by cautery or ligation, under general anaesthesia.
neetpg2021-q121: In pheochromocytoma, alpha blockade (phenoxybenzamine) must come first, then a beta blocker. Giving propranolol first causes unopposed alpha stimulation and a hypertensive crisis, so this statement is incorrect.
neetpg2021-q122: Giant cell arteritis with jaw claudication and risk of vision loss is treated immediately with high-dose glucocorticoids, to be given before biopsy. Tocilizumab is an add-on for relapse or steroid-sparing.
neetpg2021-q123: Chest pain on exertion that is increasing or at rest, with ECG changes (flat T waves) and nitrate-responsive episodes, is unstable angina, treated with antiplatelets, an anticoagulant such as enoxaparin, nitrates and beta blockers. The key marks enoxaparin.
neetpg2021-q124: A history of chronic ear disease with headache, vomiting and confusion and a ring-enhancing lesion in the temporal lobe on CT is a temporal lobe abscess. Cerebellar abscess is also otogenic but presents with ataxia.
neetpg2021-q125: The Kata thermometer measures low air velocity and the cooling power of the air (by cooling time between 100 and 95 degrees F). The globe thermometer measures radiant heat.
neetpg2021-q126: Bubonic plague (buboes) is transmitted by the rat flea, Xenopsylla cheopis, from rodents to humans.
neetpg2021-q127: A boggy, painful scalp swelling with hair loss in a child with a pet dog is a kerion, an inflammatory reaction to zoophilic dermatophytes (Microsporum canis or Trichophyton). It is treated with oral griseofulvin or terbinafine.
neetpg2021-q128: Succinylcholine (suxamethonium) with halothane can trigger malignant hyperthermia, with muscle rigidity and hyperthermia from uncontrolled calcium release through the ryanodine receptor. Treatment is dantrolene.
neetpg2021-q129: For flood-affected areas, doxycycline is given to prevent leptospirosis, and the key marks malathion as the chemical distributed along with it. This is probably a vector-control measure.
neetpg2021-q130: Follicular, horny papules on the extensor surfaces of the limbs in a child with night blindness suggest phrynoderma (toad skin), caused by vitamin A (and essential fatty acid) deficiency.
neetpg2021-q131: Blood spills are disinfected with 1% sodium hypochlorite, which is effective against HIV, hepatitis B and C. Absorb the spill first, then disinfect for 10-30 minutes.
neetpg2021-q132: Capnography (detection of end-tidal CO2) is the most reliable method to confirm tracheal placement of an endotracheal tube. Auscultation and chest rise are supportive. A chest X-ray checks depth.
neetpg2021-q133: The AQI values of the day shown fall in the severe range (AQI above 400) in the Indian National Air Quality Index.
neetpg2021-q134: The Japanese encephalitis vaccine used in India is the live attenuated SA 14-14-2 strain, given subcutaneously (0.5 mL) at 9-12 months, and a second dose at 16-24 months.
neetpg2021-q135: In a lumbar puncture the needle passes the skin, subcutaneous tissue, supraspinous and interspinous ligaments, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura and arachnoid, entering the subarachnoid space (lumbar cistern). The last layer pierced is the arachnoid.
neetpg2021-q136: In Donabedian's model, evaluation of the care actually given (clinical management of the patient) measures the process. Structure is the resources and facilities, and outcome is the result of care.
neetpg2021-q137: Flaccid, easily ruptured bullae with a suprabasal split (acantholysis) and a tombstone appearance is pemphigus vulgaris. Pemphigus foliaceus has a subcorneal split.
neetpg2021-q138: Cardiac arrest after a regional block with bupivacaine is local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST). Treatment is CPR with 20% lipid emulsion (intralipid), using reduced epinephrine doses.
neetpg2021-q139: Acute paronychia is usually Staphylococcus aureus, treated with warm soaks and oral antibiotics such as amoxicillin-clavulanate (or cloxacillin), and incision and drainage if pus has collected.
neetpg2021-q140: Worsening of lesions and new nerve involvement during MDT is a type 1 (reversal) lepra reaction. MDT is continued and systemic corticosteroids (prednisolone) are started to prevent nerve damage. Thalidomide is for ENL (type 2).
neetpg2021-q141: A small-volume, low-grade (Gleason 6), low PSA (under 10) prostate cancer in an elderly man is low-risk, so active surveillance is preferred. Radical treatment is for higher risk or longer life expectancy.

neetpg2021-q149: A hernia medial to the inferior epigastric artery is a direct inguinal hernia (through Hesselbach's triangle). Mesh repair (Lichtenstein) is the standard treatment, with lower recurrence than tissue repair (Bassini).

neetpg2021-q154: Conditioning influences for malnutrition are factors that modify the effect of the primary causes, such as infections (diarrhoea, measles, worm infestations), which lower nutrient intake and absorption. Food habits and socio-economic factors are primary determinants.

neetpg2021-q157: Oral rehydration solution works through the sodium-glucose cotransporter 1 (SGLT1) in the small intestine, which couples sodium and glucose uptake, followed by water. This is preserved in cholera and other secretory diarrhoeas.
neetpg2021-q158: A stone in the common bile duct appearing 2 years after cholecystectomy is a retained stone if it was missed at surgery (within 2 years), whereas a stone formed in the duct afterwards is a primary stone. The key marks retained.
neetpg2021-q159: Serum lipase is more specific and stays elevated longer than amylase for diagnosing acute pancreatitis. A fluid collection near the pancreas is a pseudocyst or acute collection.

neetpg2021-q172: A strict aerobe from a burn wound that is oxidase positive and produces blue-green pigment (pyocyanin) is Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The oxidase test shown is positive.

neetpg2021-q178: Spinal tuberculosis with a psoas abscess causes persistent hip flexion with painful, limited extension (psoas spasm). The marked option is the iliopsoas muscle shown in the image.

neetpg2021-q181: In a stable blunt trauma patient with abdominal tenderness, the first bedside investigation is FAST (focused assessment with sonography for trauma) for free fluid. CT is used in stable patients after that, as per the key it is FAST.

neetpg2021-q184: A baby with watering, photophobia (inability to open eyes in light) and a large hazy cornea has congenital glaucoma (buphthalmos). Treatment is surgical, with goniotomy or trabeculotomy.
